transferPolicyReview.residencyNote: The standard 15-credit eligible-course residency remains separate from university-only SOS-1100 and LIB-4950; military and Edison Accelerate use their own policies.

courseCreditExclusions.notes: TESU does not award credit for both technical-writing courses. The English choice row permits either; their identities are not aliases.

rulesNotes: The six English-elective courses are proposed named undergraduate ENG/LIT subject choices within the published 18-credit English-elective allowance. They are not asserted to be a university-mandated six-course list or a transfer award.
Current English and Literature catalog families establish the selected subjects, quantities, levels and online availability. No historical catalog is treated as current approval.
The baseline selects the published SOC-2910 and HIS-1140 Human Cultures options, avoiding a TECEP-only PHI-1300 fallback.
MAT-1050 is the current published featured quantitative-literacy course.
No course is counted both in general education, English, Humanities or unrestricted electives.
The degree is not represented as a teacher licensure or professional-practice qualification.

MAN-3730 is explicitly listed in the university Humanities taxonomy. It is a proposed Humanities allocation; its existing Study.com receiving award retains its original conditional evidence rather than becoming a new English-specific transfer guarantee.
The 18 upper-level area-of-study credits cannot be replaced by upper-level free electives.
The formal ENC-1020 prerequisites for LIT-4600, LIT-3010, LIT-3020 and LIT-3310 are separate from advisory composition and literature background.
LIT-2910 is retained at its published 2000-level code; its advisory wording does not establish a 3000-level credit award.
LIB-4950 has a near-completion advisory, without an invented numeric prerequisite.
The standard 15-credit residency, derived 105-credit outside ceiling and 90-credit combined alternative ceiling are separate.
A business-specific course-age policy is not copied into this B.A. English plan.
pricingNotes: Published standard tuition is a provisional planning basis; provider subscriptions, books and applicable fees are separate.
